name: Parking Ramp
desc: A helical parking deck driven forever — the camera corkscrews and climbs so the whole structure banks around it, mushroom columns and sodium tubes whip past, and daylight cuts through the spandrel slots between the parapet and the deck one turn overhead.

energy.doc: tube output, headlamp wash, camera drift and climb rate

scale.doc: deck depth + storey height (2.2 = a cavernous deck; the helix radius and eye height stay fixed so this is never a no-op)

density.doc: how far around the helix you can see — 1 reveals well past a full turn

speed.doc: rate the camera drives the ramp (this is also the rate the frame rotates)

hue.doc: daylight/lamp hue; concrete takes its complement

decay.doc: rust bleed and water staining down the spandrels

style.doc: aesthetic: cool board-formed concrete / amber sodium night / rust-bled decay / cyan schematic linework / hatched paper plate

seed.doc: weathering, dead tubes, stain placement (absolute-segment keyed, so no two turns of the helix repeat)
